issues.claim: Начиная с C# 8 ... switch-выражение с шаблонами типов
issues.problem: Switch expressions arrived in C# 8, but the bare type pattern (`Circle => ...`) arrived in C# 9. In C# 8 the same dispatch is written with a declaration pattern (`Circle c => ...`). The claim is loosely true but imprecise.
issues.suggestedFix: Write 'Since C# 8 (type patterns without a variable since C# 9)', or say 'switch expression with type patterns' without tying it to C# 8.

issues.claim: C# 14 has no closed hierarchies; a node's Update method returns the same object when children are unchanged; CSharpSyntaxVisitor and CSharpSyntaxRewriter exist
issues.problem: These claims are true from my knowledge, but none is shown in the fetched excerpts and the Roslyn types have no link. The fetched switch-expression page already documents union types, which belong to a newer C# version, so a reader may be confused about C# 14.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a short note that unions and closed hierarchies are not part of C# 14. Optionally add a Roslyn syntax visitor link and cite the Expression.Update documentation.
